analysis.investment_thesis: Fedbank Financial Services is a fast-growing NBFC with 32% revenue CAGR, but its ROE of 8.84% is well below my 15% threshold and profits actually declined in FY2025 (₹245 Cr → ₹225 Cr) despite 30% revenue growth — a classic warning sign of margin deterioration. At D/E of 3.83 with no demonstrated pricing power or durable moat, this is a leveraged commodity lender, not a compounding machine.
key_strengths: Federal Bank parentage (60.79% promoter stake) provides funding access and regulatory credibility
Strong top-line momentum: revenue CAGR of 32.2% from ₹854 Cr to ₹1,973 Cr over three years
Forward P/E of 11.35 offers some valuation cushion if asset quality holds and margins recover
key_risks: ROE of 8.84% and ROCE of 12.40% fail the quality hurdle — this business destroys value at the margin relative to its cost of equity
FY2025 earnings contraction (net profit -8% YoY, EBITDA -7% YoY) while AUM grew 19%, pointing to rising credit costs or NIM compression
D/E of 3.83 with 100% negative free cash flow history (0/4 years positive OCF) means survival depends on continuous external financing — dangerous in a credit tightening cycle
red_flags: Profit declined in FY2025 despite 30% revenue growth — operating leverage is running in reverse
Near-zero FII ownership (0.66%) signals institutional smart money has no conviction here
Persistently negative FCF every single year (-₹605, -₹1,489, -₹789, -₹996 Cr) — the business consumes capital relentlessly
No disclosed NPA/GNPA data; margin compression without asset quality context is a black box
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Invert first: what would make this a terrible investment? A leveraged NBFC with sub-10% ROE, shrinking profits, no pricing power, zero free cash flow, and a business model indistinguishable from dozens of competitors. That is precisely what Fedbank Financial Services looks like today. The 32% revenue CAGR is impressive on the surface, but growth without returns is a treadmill — the company raised equity in FY2024 (equity jumped from ₹1,356 Cr to ₹2,261 Cr) and still managed to earn only 8.84% ROE. A business that can't earn above its cost of capital while borrowing at 3.83x equity is consuming, not creating, shareholder wealth.

The FY2025 data is the most alarming signal: revenue grew 30% to ₹1,973 Cr yet net profit fell 8% to ₹225 Cr. This scissors pattern — expanding book, shrinking bottom line — typically means rising credit costs (provisions eating into NIM) or funding cost pressure. Without NPA disclosures in this dataset, it's a black box, and I refuse to invest in black boxes. The competitive dynamics of Indian NBFC lending are brutal — gold loans, LAP, SME loans are all contested by banks, fintechs, and dozens of specialized lenders. There is no moat here, only leverage. Pass.
